about: The one source of 'why' and 'how long' for setup. install: one entry per item the install script can plan; the script prints the why and the minutes with every plan row. steps: the guide's steps, in order; part is 1 (the guide) or 2 (the extras page), a null minutes shows no time, choices lists the only keys a step may record in core_text/setup.json, explain gives one line per option for a step (or, on engine-env, the judge question) that asks the user to choose (what they gain or lose with each), and verify is the one place the user can check the step themselves. installer/nc_setup.py, bin/setup_record.py and the setup skill all read this file, so adding an item or a step is an edit here.

install.title: Claude Code's command line
install.why: Installing Claude Code's command line so your team can be installed and updated reliably.

install.title: Git
install.why: Installing Git so your team can tell exactly what changed in your project.
install.why_windows: Installing Git because you're on Windows: it gives your team the command line its safety checks run in.

install.title: Python
install.why: Installing Python so your team's memory and safety checks can run.

install.title: jq
install.why: Installing jq so your team's guardrails can read what's happening in a session.

install.why: Checking that this computer can reach GitHub, where your team is downloaded from.

install.why: Creating a folder just for this project, so your team's files stay in one place and your other folders stay as they are.

install.title: Your team
install.why: Installing your team, and Hyperspace Engine with it.

install.title: Hyperspace Engine's workspace
install.why: Building Hyperspace Engine's private workspace, where your task graph and its checks run.
install.judge: When a task is finished, a judge reads what it had to achieve and the evidence, and says whether it is really done; it uses Claude Code's command line on your Claude plan. No judge turns it off, and you can switch it on or off later.
explain: Judge on (our recommendation): a task closes only when Claude agrees the evidence shows it is done, and each check uses a little of your Claude plan.
No judge: a task closes on its file and command checks alone, which costs nothing, but nobody reads whether the work really does what the task asked.

install.title: Obsidian check
install.why: Checking whether Obsidian is installed, so setup can offer it without asking you to look.

steps.title: Quick questions and the basics
steps.does: Asks what to call your project and where it should live, then checks this computer, installs only what's missing, and creates your project folder with your team in it.
steps.why: Your team needs a folder of its own and a few free tools before it can start.
steps.if_skipped: Not skippable: without these your team can't start.
explain: The Projects folder in your home folder (our default): kept apart from anything that syncs, so a workspace with thousands of files stays fast.
A folder you already have: fine too, and your team's files go in beside yours. A folder that syncs, such as OneDrive, slows the workspace down.
steps.verify: Open your project folder to see it, and run “claude plugin list” in a terminal in that folder: your team, technical-cofounder, is on the list.

steps.title: This guide
steps.does: Every step, how long it takes, and what can wait.
steps.why: See the whole path, then do what fits today.
steps.verify: This page is a file in your project: core_text/setup-guide.html. Open it again any time.

steps.title: Where you read and edit Markdown
steps.does: Picks the app you'll open Markdown (.md) files in: we recommend Obsidian, and VS Code, Typora or Zed work too.
steps.why: Almost every file your agents read and write is Markdown, from your profile and plans to the worklog, rules and skills: it's the core file type here, not “notes”.
steps.if_skipped: Choosing TextEdit (Mac) or Notepad (Windows) counts as done: they open Markdown as raw text, with no formatting, links or search.
explain: Obsidian: free and our pick. Links, search and a worklog table, and the next step builds on it. You learn one more app.
VS Code or Zed: free editors that show Markdown well. No vault view or worklog table.
Typora: paid, the cleanest reading view. No vault view or worklog table.
TextEdit or Notepad: already on your computer. Plain text only, with no formatting, links or search.
steps.verify: Open your profile, core_text/user.md, in the app you chose: if it opens and reads well, you're set.

steps.title: Obsidian (recommended)
steps.does: Opens this project as an Obsidian vault, with a ready-made worklog table and a short how-to (OBSIDIAN.md).
steps.why: Your whole project, every file and link, in one searchable place instead of a folder of files.
steps.if_skipped: Everything still works in your editor, without the vault view or the worklog table.
explain: Yes: your project opens as one searchable vault, and your worklog (the team's diary: one short file per piece of work, so the next session knows what happened) also shows as one table. You learn one more app.
No: nothing breaks. The worklog files still land in worklog/ and Hyperspace Engine's console shows them in its worklog tab, without the vault view or the table. You can switch later.
steps.verify: In Obsidian, choose “Open folder as vault” and pick your project folder: worklog/worklog.base shows your worklog as a table.

steps.title: GitHub (optional, strongly recommended)
steps.does: Connects this computer to a free GitHub account with GitHub's command-line tool. It takes about 5 minutes with an account, longer without.
steps.why: Every change is backed up off this computer and can be undone; it solves backup and lost-file problems for good, and it's free.
steps.if_skipped: Your project lives only on this computer, one lost laptop or bad edit away from gone; add it any time.
explain: Yes: every change is backed up off this computer and can be undone. About 5 minutes with an account, and free.
Not now: your project lives only on this computer, one lost laptop or bad edit away from gone. You can add GitHub any time.
steps.verify: github.com/settings/applications lists GitHub CLI under Authorized OAuth Apps: that is this computer's login.

steps.title: Your starter workspace
steps.does: Adds your profile, worklog, rules and templates to this project.
steps.why: It's how every agent remembers you and what happened last session.
steps.if_skipped: Not skippable: the rest of setup writes into these files.
steps.verify: Open your project folder: core_text/user.md, CLAUDE.md, worklog/ and _templates/ are there now.

steps.title: What to try first
steps.does: Three things to try first. No run is open yet: every piece of work starts at Understand.
steps.why: A small first win shows how the team works.
steps.verify: Hyperspace Engine's console shows every task and run in your browser: ask your team to open it.

steps.title: About you
steps.does: A short interview that fills in your profile.
steps.why: Agents read it every session, so they work your way from the first message.
steps.if_skipped: Agents use general defaults and won't know your goals or style.
explain: A test drive: you try the team on something small first and see how it works. Nothing has to be decided yet.
I know what I'm building: the team starts on your real project straight away.
Desktop app or command line (CLI): your team can't see which one you use, so it gives you the steps for yours. Both work the same.
steps.verify: Your answers are in core_text/user.md: open it to read or change any of them.

steps.title: Research extras (optional)
steps.does: Three services for your agents: web research (Exa), live library docs (Context7) and a cloud browser (Browserbase).
steps.why: Agents check today's docs and the web instead of guessing from memory.
steps.if_skipped: Agents use built-in web search; anything that needs a real browser comes back to you.
steps.cost: Free tiers; you create the accounts
explain: Yes: web research with sources (Exa), live library docs (Context7) and a cloud browser for pages that need clicks or a login (Browserbase). About 15 minutes, on free tiers, with your own accounts.
Not now: agents use Claude Code's built-in web search and fetch, and anything that needs a real browser comes back to you.
steps.verify: In a session in your project, type /mcp: context7, exa and browserbase are listed, marked as coming from a plugin.
